---
title: "Methods Teaching Resources"
toc: false
---

A collection of short videos, slide decks, and class activities for teaching introductory research methods and quantitative analysis in the social sciences. The materials were developed for an undergraduate Statistics module in Politics at King's College London, and are designed to be modular: individual videos, slides, or activities can be reused or adapted for related courses without adopting the full module structure.

Each topic combines short concept videos, slide decks, and a class activity. Concept videos focus on intuition and pedagogy, and are designed to be software-agnostic. Applied videos illustrate how each idea translates into practical data work in Stata. The intent is to support flipped and blended teaching: students prepare with the videos before class, and in-person time is used for active work on activities and applications.

The materials are intended to be adaptable for colleagues teaching research design, introductory quantitative methods, and applied data analysis. Individual pieces can be picked up without committing to the full sequence.

Materials developed by [Leonardo Falabella](https://falabella.quarto.pub/) (leonardo.falabella@kcl.ac.uk).
